thread.title: Like a Bad Neighbor, State Farm Ain't There: Refuses to Pay Out Fire Victims For Personal Property Without Detailed Inventory List
thread.title_full: Like a Bad Neighbor, State Farm Ain't There: Refuses to Pay Out Fire Victims For Personal Property Without Detailed Inventory List

author: Chris_K
text: There seems to be confusion on what is being described here. They are not saying you have to have a premade list. You have to make a list for the insurance adjuster of the items. They don't just pay you a blanket policy limit without you itemizing a list of what was damaged. Very normal insurance procedure. The State of CA is trying to make them pay 100% without even having policy holders make a list. Lots of people are over insured on contents, so a list to justify your amount is reasonable. If CA wants them to pay 100%, then make CA a valued policy state by law, and the companies will have to pay 100% in a total loss and the insurance companies can adjust their premium accordingly ahead of time based on the law. As usual, CA democrats want something for free..
